properties.title: Countess Pillar, Brougham
properties.description: A monument erected in 1656 by Lady Anne Clifford of nearby Brougham Castle, to commemorate her final parting here from her mother.

properties.title: Cow Tower, Norwich
properties.description: One of the earliest purpose-built artillery blockhouses in England, this brick tower was built in c.1398-9 to command a strategic point in Norwich’s city defence.

properties.title: Creake Abbey
properties.description: The ruined church of an Augustinian abbey, reduced in size after fire and plague.

properties.title: Cromwell's Castle
properties.description: The castle stands guarding the lovely anchorage between Bryher and Tresco and is one of the few surviving Cromwellian fortifications in Britain.

properties.title: Croxden Abbey
properties.description: The impressive remains of an abbey of Cistercian 'white monks', including towering fragments of its 13th-century church, infirmary and 14th-century abbot's lodging.

properties.title: Dartmouth Castle
properties.description: A stunning waterfront fortress

properties.title: Daw's Castle
properties.description: Daw's Castle is a clifftop fortress, which was founded by King Alfred to defend the people of Watchet against Viking attacks.
properties.period_detail: Early Medieval (c. 410 - 1066 AD: Anglo-Saxon / Celtic / Viking)

properties.title: De Grey Mausoleum, Flitton
properties.description: Among the largest sepulchral chapels attached to any English church, this cruciform mausoleum houses a remarkable sequence of 17 sculpted and effigied monuments.
properties.period_detail: 17th Century (begun 1614 sepulchral chapel, Earls of Kent)

properties.title: Deal Castle
properties.description: Devilish defences at one of Henry VIII’s finest artillery forts

properties.title: Deddington Castle
properties.description: Extensive earthworks marking the site of an 11th century motte and bailey castle.

properties.title: Denny Abbey and the Farmland Museum
properties.description: Denny Abbey has a unique and fascinating history still traceable in the building and interpreted for visitors by graphic panels.

properties.title: Denton Hall Turret - Hadrian's Wall
properties.description: The foundations of a turret and a 65-metre (213 foot) length of Wall, along with another 60-metre length of Wall further west.

properties.title: Derwentcote Steel Furnace
properties.description: Built in the 1720s, Derwentcote is the earliest and most complete steel-making furnace in Britain. It produced high-grade steel for springs and cutting tools.

properties.title: Donnington Castle
properties.description: The striking twin-towered 14th-century gatehouse of this castle, later the focus of a Civil War siege and battle, survives amid impressive earthworks.

properties.title: Dover Castle
properties.description: High atop the iconic White Cliffs of Dover sits the most iconic of all English fortresses. From the mighty medieval keep to the labyrinth of secret wartime tunnels below, a family day out at Dover towers above all others.

properties.title: Dunstanburgh Castle
properties.description: Dramatic ruins on the wild Northumberland coast

properties.title: Dunster Butter Cross
properties.description: Transplanted stump of a medieval stone cross that was once a meeting place for people to bring and sell their own butter. Nearby attractions include Cleeve Abbey.

properties.title: Dunster Gallox Bridge
properties.description: This ancient stone bridge - originally 'gallows bridge' - once carried packhorses bringing fleeces to Dunster market and is evidence of Dunster's once important role in the wool trade.

properties.title: Dunster, Yarn Market
properties.description: Fine 17th century timber-framed octagonal market hall that is a monument to Dunster's once-flourishing cloth trade.

properties.title: Dupath Well
properties.description: This charming well-house of around 1500 stands over an ancient spring, believed to cure whooping cough.

properties.title: Duxford Chapel
properties.description: A modest but complete and attractive 14th-century chantry chapel, perhaps originally a hospital.

properties.title: Dymchurch Martello Tower
properties.description: This is one of a chain of ingeniously designed artillery towers built around the south and east coasts of England from 1805 to protect against the threat of invasion by Napoleon.

properties.title: Easby Abbey
properties.description: In a beautiful setting by the River Swale, Easby can be reached via a pleasant walk from Richmond Castle.
properties.locationText: North Yorkshire, Yorkshire and the Humber

properties.title: Edlingham Castle
properties.description: The riverside ruins, principally the solar tower, of a manor house progressively fortified against the Scots during the 14th century.

properties.title: Edvin Loach Old Church
properties.description: The ruins of an 11th century and later church built within the earthworks of a Norman motte and bailey castle, with a Victorian church nearby. The site of hundreds of years of worship.

properties.title: Egglestone Abbey
properties.description: The charming ruins of a small monastery of Premonstratensian 'white canons', picturesquely set above a bend in the River Tees near Barnard Castle.

properties.title: Eleanor Cross, Geddington
properties.description: In 1290 Eleanor of Castile, the beloved wife of Edward I and mother of his 14 children, died at Harby in Nottinghamshire.

properties.title: Eltham Palace and Gardens
properties.description: Millionaire life in an art deco mansion
properties.period_detail: Medieval Royal Palace & 1930s Art Deco mansion

properties.title: Etal Castle
properties.description: Etal was built in the mid 14th century by Robert Manners as a defence against Scots raiders, in a strategic position by a ford over the river Till.

properties.title: Eynsford Castle
properties.description: The substantial stone walls of a very early Norman 'enclosure castle', begun c.1085-7 and unusually little altered by later building works. This rare survival stands in an attractive village setting.

properties.title: Farleigh Hungerford Castle
properties.description: Mysterious tales and a creepy chapel crypt

properties.title: Farnham Castle Keep
properties.description: The impressive motte and shell keep of Farnham Castle, Surrey, founded in 1138 by Bishop Henry of Blois. An enjoyable day out within travelling distance of London.

properties.title: Faversham Stone Chapel (Our Lady of Elverton)
properties.description: The ruins of the small Anglo-Saxon and medieval chapel of Stone-next-Faversham.
properties.period_detail: Early Medieval (c. 410 - 1066 AD: Anglo-Saxon / Celtic / Viking)

properties.title: Fiddleford Manor
properties.description: The principal parts of a small stone manor house, probably begun about 1370 for William Latimer, Sheriff of Somerset and Dorset. The hall and solar chamber display outstandingly fine timber roofs.

properties.title: Finchale Priory
properties.description: The very extensive remains of a 13th-century priory, founded on the site of a retired pirate's hermitage. Part of it later served as a holiday retreat for the monks of Durham Cathedral.

properties.title: Flowerdown Barrows
properties.description: Three Bronze Age burial mounds, once part of a much larger 'barrow cemetery', including two bowl barrows, and the largest and finest disc barrow in Hampshire.

properties.title: Fort Brockhurst
properties.description: One of a number of forts built in the 1850s and 1860s to protect Portsmouth and its harbour against a French invasion. Largely unaltered, the parade ground, gun ramps and moated keep can be viewed.

properties.title: Framlingham Castle
properties.description: One of medieval England’s finest baronial fortresses, with plenty to see and do.

properties.title: Furness Abbey
properties.description: The North West’s most majestic abbey ruins, now with a recreated monks’ eye view.

properties.title: Gainsborough Old Hall
properties.description: Discover one of England’s biggest – yet least known – medieval manor houses

properties.title: Gainsthorpe Medieval Village
properties.description: A deserted medieval village, one of the best-preserved examples in England, clearly visible as a complex of grassy humps and bumps.

properties.title: Garrison Walls
properties.description: You can enjoy a two-hour walk alongside the ramparts of these defensive walls and earthworks, dating from the 16th to 18th centuries.

properties.title: Gisborough Priory
properties.description: The ruins of an Augustinian priory founded by the Bruce family, afterwards Kings of Scotland. They are dominated by the dramatic skeleton of the 14th-century church's east end.
properties.locationText: North Yorkshire, Yorkshire and the Humber

properties.title: Glastonbury Tribunal
properties.description: Fine, late 15th century stone townhouse, early Tudor façade and panelled interiors. Home to Glastonbury Lake Village Exhibition: discover life 2000 years ago when much of Somerset consisted of marshy sea.

properties.title: Goodrich Castle
properties.description: Medieval life in a picturesque and powerful stronghold

properties.title: Goodshaw Chapel
properties.description: English Heritage's only Nonconformist place of worship, this atmospheric Baptist chapel displays a complete set of box-pews, galleries and pulpit dating from c. 1742 to 1809.

properties.title: Great Witcombe Roman Villa
properties.description: The remains of a large and luxurious villa built about AD 250, with a bathhouse complex, perhaps the shrine of a water spirit, and mosaics.

properties.title: Great Yarmouth Row Houses and Greyfriars' Cloisters
properties.description: Vividly presented evocations of life in a fishing port, open again after conservation
properties.period_detail: 14th Century medieval alley houses & 13th C friary

properties.title: Greyfriars
properties.description: Substantial remains of an early Tudor friary church of Franciscan 'grey friars' founded in 1231.

properties.title: Grime's Graves - Prehistoric Flint Mine
properties.description: Visit Grime’s Graves and explore Britain’s only open Neolithic flint mine.

properties.title: Grimspound
properties.description: The best known of many Dartmoor prehistoric settlements, Grimspound dates from the late Bronze Age. The remains of 24 stone houses survive within a massive boundary wall.

properties.title: Hadleigh Castle
properties.description: The romantic ruins of a royal castle overlooking the Essex marshes. Hadleigh was begun in about 1215 by Hubert de Burgh, but extensively refortified by Edward III during the Hundred Years War.

properties.title: Hadrian's Wall
properties.description: Hadrian’s Wall was the north-west frontier of the Roman empire for nearly 300 years. At 73 miles it marches across northern Britain from sea to sea. The most famous of all the frontiers of the Roman empire, Hadrian’s Wall was made a World Heritage Site in 1987.

properties.title: Hailes Abbey
properties.description: Home of the Holy Blood

properties.title: Halesowen Abbey
properties.description: Remains of abbey founded by King John in the 13th century.

properties.title: Halliggye Fogou
properties.description: Roofed and walled in stone, this complex of passages is the largest and best-preserved of several mysterious underground tunnels associated with Cornish Iron Age settlements.

properties.title: Hardknott Roman Fort
properties.description: This remote and dramatically sited fort was founded under Hadrian's rule in the 2nd century. Well-marked remains include the headquarters building, commandant's house and bath house.

properties.title: Hardwick Old Hall and Hardwick Hall
properties.description: Two great Elizabethan mansions, side by side.

properties.title: Hare Hill - Hadrian's Wall
properties.description: A short length of Wall, still standing 2.7 metres (8.8 feet) high.

properties.title: Harmondsworth Barn
properties.description: This Grade I listed oak-framed medieval barn ranks alongside the Houses of Parliament, Westminster Abbey and Buckingham Palace for its exceptional architectural and historic interest.

properties.title: Harrows Scar Milecastle and Wall - Hadrian's Wall
properties.description: A mile-long section of the Wall, rebuilt in stone later in Hadrian's reign. It is linked to Birdoswald Roman Fort.

properties.title: Harry's Walls
properties.description: An unfinished artillery fort, built above St Mary's Pool harbour in 1552-53.

properties.title: Hatfield Earthworks (Marden Henge)
properties.description: The earthworks of a Neolithic henge and monumental mound, by a loop in the River Avon. Recent archaeological find of building equivalent to a priest’s quarters.

properties.title: Haughmond Abbey
properties.description: Extensive remains of Augustinian abbey, including abbots' quarters, refectory & cloister. Chapter house frontage with 12th & 14th century carving & statuary, timber roof c.1500. Displays, picnic area.

properties.title: Heddon on the Wall  Hadrian's Wall
properties.description: A consolidated stretch of Wall, up to 2 metres (6.6 feet) thick in places.

properties.title: Helmsley Archaeology Store
properties.description: Helmsley Archaeology Store holds the extensive archaeological collections and paper based archives from English Heritage guardianship sites from the North of England including the counties of Northumberland, County Durham, Cumbria, Lancashire, Yorkshire, North Lincolnshire, Cheshire.

properties.title: Helmsley Castle
properties.description: Explore the story of a great castle across nine centuries
properties.locationText: North Yorkshire, Yorkshire and the Humber

properties.title: Hill Hall
properties.description: This fine Elizabethan mansion features some of the earliest external Renaissance architectural detail in the country.

properties.title: Hob Hurst's House
properties.description: A square prehistoric burial mound with an earthwork ditch and outer bank. Named after a local goblin.

properties.title: Home of Charles Darwin - Down House
properties.description: The great scientist’s country-house home and ‘outdoor laboratory’

properties.title: Horne's Place Chapel
properties.description: A rare survival of a fine domestic chapel, built for William Horne in 1366 and attached to his timber-framed manor house, which was attacked during the Peasants' Revolt of 1381.
properties.period_detail: 14th Century (1366 domestic chapel for William Horne)

properties.title: Houghton House
properties.description: Houghton House today is the shell of a 17th century mansion commanding magnificent views, reputedly the inspiration for the ‘House Beautiful’ in John Bunyan’s Pilgrim’s Progress.

properties.title: Hound Tor Deserted Medieval Village
properties.description: The remains of four 13th century stone farmsteads, on land originally farmed in the Bronze Age. This isolated Dartmoor hamlet was probably abandoned in the early 15th century.

properties.title: Housesteads Roman Fort - Hadrian's Wall
properties.description: Britain’s most complete Roman fort, in a spectacular landscape.

properties.title: Howden Minster
properties.description: The elaborately decorated ruins of a 14th-century chancel and chapter house (viewable only from the outside), attached to the still operational cathedral-like minster church.
properties.locationText: East Yorkshire, Yorkshire and the Humber

properties.title: Hurlers Stone Circles
properties.description: Three fine late Neolithic or early Bronze Age stone circles arranged in a line, a grouping unique in England.

properties.title: Hurst Castle
properties.description: Hurst Castle provides a remote escape by the sea with plenty of things to do and see! Built by Henry VIII; one of the most advanced artillery fortresses in England.

properties.title: Hylton Castle
properties.description: The distinctive and highly decorative gatehouse-tower of a castle built by the wealthy Sir William Hylton, shortly before 1400. Originally containing four floors of self-contained family.

properties.title: Innisidgen Lower and Upper Burial Chambers
properties.description: Two Bronze Age communal burial cairns of Scillonian type, with fine views. The upper cairn is the best preserved on the islands.

properties.title: Iron Bridge
properties.description: The world’s first iron bridge was erected over the River Severn here in 1779 by Abraham Darby III. Costing over £6000, the bridge was cast in his Coalbrookdale foundry, using 378 tons of iron.

properties.title: Isleham Priory Church
properties.description: Isleham Priory Church is the best example in England of a small Norman Benedictine priory church, surviving in a surprisingly unaltered state despite later conversion into a barn.

properties.title: JW Evans Silver Factory
properties.description: A treasure trove of industry frozen in time.

properties.title: Jewel Tower
properties.description: A hidden treasury in the heart of London
properties.period_detail: 14th Century (1365, Edward III Palace of Westminster)

properties.title: Jewry Wall
properties.description: A length of Roman bath-house wall over 9 metres (30 feet) high, near a museum displaying the archaeology of Leicester and its region.

properties.title: Jordan Hill Roman Temple
properties.description: The foundations of a 4th century Romano-Celtic temple with fine coastal views.

properties.title: Kenilworth Castle and Elizabethan Garden
properties.description: Medieval fortress turned showstopper Elizabethan palace

properties.title: Kenwood
properties.description: This outstanding house beside Hampstead Heath was remodelled by Robert Adam between 1764 and 1779. He transformed the original brick building into a majestic villa for the great judge, Lord Mansfield.

properties.title: King Arthur's Round Table
properties.description: A Neolithic earthwork henge, dating from c. 2000 BC, but much later believed to be King Arthur's jousting arena. Mayburgh Henge is adjacent.

properties.title: King Charles's Castle
properties.description: The ruins of a mid 16th century coastal artillery fort, later garrisoned - hence the name - by Civil War Royalists.

properties.title: King Doniert's Stone
properties.description: Two richly carved pieces of a 9th century 'Celtic' cross, with an inscription commemorating Dumgarth, British King of Dumnonia, who drowned in c. AD 875.

properties.title: King James's and Landport Gates, Portsmouth
properties.description: Two ornamental gateways, once part of Portsmouth's defences. King James's Gate (of 1687) has been moved, but Landport Gate (1760), remains in it's original position.

properties.title: Kingston Russell Stone Circle
properties.description: A late Neolithic or early Bronze Age circle of 18 fallen stones, on a hilltop overlooking Abbotsbury and the sea.

properties.title: Kingswood Abbey Gatehouse
properties.description: This 16th century gatehouse, one of the latest monastic buildings in England, displays a richly sculpted mullioned window. It is the sole survivor of this Cistercian abbey.

properties.title: Kirby Hall
properties.description: Trace the rise and fall of a great Elizabethan and Stuart mansion.

properties.title: Kirby Muxloe Castle
properties.description: The unfinished showpiece mansion of a royal favourite – and royal victim

properties.title: Kirkham House, Paignton
properties.description: This late medieval stone house, afterwards split into three cottages was restored in the 1960s.

properties.title: Kirkham Priory
properties.description: Idyllic riverside ruins with a surprising recent history
properties.locationText: North Yorkshire, Yorkshire and the Humber

properties.title: Kit's Coty House and Little Kit's Coty House
properties.description: The remains of two megalithic 'dolmen' burial chambers. Impressive Kit's Coty has three uprights and a massive capstone: Little Kit's Coty, alias the Countless Stones, is now a jumble of sarsens.

properties.title: Knights Templar Church, Dover
properties.description: The foundations of a small medieval church, traditionally said to have been the site of King John's submission to the Papal Legate in 1213.

properties.title: Knowlton Church and Earthworks
properties.description: The siting of this ruined medieval church at the centre of a Neolithic ritual henge earthwork symbolises the transition from pagan to Christian worship and creates an atmospheric scene.

properties.title: Landguard Fort
properties.description: Landguard Fort is the site of the last opposed seaborne invasion of England in 1667 and the first land battle of the Royal Marines.

properties.title: Lanercost Priory
properties.description: An impressive and now-tranquil priory, once in the Anglo-Scottish firing line.

properties.title: Langley Chapel
properties.description: A small chapel tranquilly set all alone in charming countryside. Its atmospheric interior contains a perfect set of 17th-century timber furnishings, including a musicians' pew.

properties.title: Launceston Castle
properties.description: Stunning views from Cornwall’s most important medieval fortress

properties.title: Leahill Turret and Piper Sike Turret - Hadrian's Wall
properties.description: Turrets west of Birdoswald: Piper Sike has a cooking-hearth.

properties.title: Leigh Court Barn
properties.description: An outstanding display of English medieval carpentry, this mighty timber-framed barn is the largest cruck structure in Britain.

properties.title: Leiston Abbey
properties.description: The mainly 14th century remains of an abbey of Premonstratensian canons. Among Suffolk’s most impressive monastic ruins, with some spectacular architectural features.

properties.title: Lexden Earthworks and Bluebottle Grove
properties.description: The banks and ditches of a series of late Iron Age defences protecting the western side of Camulodunum – pre-Roman Colchester.

properties.title: Lilleshall Abbey
properties.description: Extensive ruins of an Augustinian abbey, later a Civil War stronghold, in a deeply rural setting.

properties.title: Lincoln Medieval Bishops' Palace
properties.description: See how we’ve safeguarded the home of Lincoln’s medieval bishops.

properties.title: Lindisfarne Priory
properties.description: England’s holy island.
properties.period_detail: Early Christian & Medieval monastery (635 AD / Norman)

properties.title: Lindsey St James's Chapel
properties.description: A pretty thatched 13th century chapel with lancet windows.

properties.title: London Wall
properties.description: This is the best-preserved remnant of the Roman wall which once formed part of the eastern defences of Roman Londinium.

properties.title: Longthorpe Tower
properties.description: Longthorpe Tower displays one of the most complete and important sets of 14th century domestic wall paintings in northern Europe.

properties.title: Longtown Castle
properties.description: A powerful thick-walled round keep of c.1150 on a large earthen mound within a stone-walled bailey. Set in the beautiful Olchon valley, with magnificent views of the Black Mountains.

properties.title: Ludgershall Castle and Cross
properties.description: The ruins and earthworks of a royal castle dating mainly from the 12th and 13th centuries, frequently used as a hunting lodge. The remains of the medieval cross stand in the centre of the village.

properties.title: Lullingstone Roman Villa
properties.description: Luxury living in Roman Britain

properties.title: Lulworth Castle
properties.description: A striking Jacobean hunting lodge on the Dorset coast.

properties.title: Lyddington Bede House
properties.description: Discover how poor men and women from the past lived in a picturesque historic almshouse
properties.period_detail: Medieval Bishop's palace turned Elizabethan almshouse

properties.title: Lydford Castle and Saxon Town
properties.description: Beautifully sited on the fringe of Dartmoor, Lydford boasts three defensive features. Near the centre is a 13th-century tower on a mound, built as a prison.
properties.period_detail: Early Medieval (c. 410 - 1066 AD: Anglo-Saxon / Celtic / Viking)

properties.title: Maiden Castle
properties.description: Among the largest and most complex Iron Age hillforts in Europe, Maiden Castle’s huge multiple ramparts enclose an area the size of 50 football pitches.

properties.title: Maison Dieu
properties.description: Originating as a 13th-century wayside hospital, this flint and timber-framed building now displays Roman artefacts from nearby sites.

properties.title: Marble Hill
properties.description: Marble Hill is the last complete survivor of the elegant villas and gardens which bordered the Thames between Richmond and Hampton Court in the 18th century.

properties.title: Marmion Tower
properties.description: The fine 15th-century gatehouse of a vanished riverside manor house, with a beautiful oriel window. The monuments of the manor's Marmion family owners grace the adjacent church.
properties.locationText: North Yorkshire, Yorkshire and the Humber

properties.title: Mattersey Priory
properties.description: The remains, mainly the 13th century refectory and kitchen, of a small monastery for just six Gilbertine canons - the only wholly English monastic order.

properties.title: Mayburgh Henge
properties.description: A large and impressive Neolithic henge, much better preserved than neighbouring King Arthur's Round Table.

properties.title: Meare Fish House
properties.description: The only surviving monastic fishery building in England, this housed the Abbot of Glastonbury's water bailiff and provided facilities for fish-salting and drying.

properties.title: Medieval Merchant's House
properties.description: Step into the recreated world of a medieval merchant

properties.title: Merrivale Prehistoric Settlement
properties.description: The group of monuments at Merrivale is one of the finest on Dartmoor: side by side here are the remains of a Bronze Age settlement and a complex of ritual sites.

properties.title: Middleham Castle
properties.description: The mighty remains of Richard III’s northern power base.
properties.locationText: North Yorkshire, Yorkshire and the Humber

properties.title: Milton Chantry
properties.description: Milton Chantry is all that remains of a 14th-century hospital later used in turn as a public house, a Georgian barracks, and Second World War gas decontamination chamber.

properties.title: Minster Lovell Hall and Dovecote
properties.description: The extensive and picturesque ruins of a 15th century riverside manor house, including a fine hall, south-west tower, and complete dovecote nearby. The home of Richard III's henchman Lord Lovell.

properties.title: Mistley Towers
properties.description: Two porticoed Classical towers, which stood at each end of a grandiose but highly unconventional Georgian church, designed by Robert Adam in 1776.

properties.title: Mitchell's Fold Stone Circle
properties.description: A Bronze Age stone circle, the focus of many legends, set in dramatic moorland on Stapeley Hill. It once consisted of some 30 stones, 15 of which are still visible.

properties.title: Monk Bretton Priory
properties.description: The substantial ruins of a Cluniac monastery, with an unusually well-marked ground plan, an almost complete west range and a 15th-century gatehouse.
properties.locationText: South Yorkshire, Yorkshire and the Humber

properties.title: Moreton Corbet Castle
properties.description: The ruins of the medieval castle and Tudor manor house of the Corbets are dominated by the theatrical shell of an ambitious Elizabethan mansion wing in Italianate style.

properties.title: Moulton Packhorse Bridge
properties.description: A pretty four-arched late medieval bridge, spanning the River Kennett on the old route from Cambridge to Bury St Edmunds.

properties.title: Mount Grace Priory, House and Gardens
properties.description: Glorious arts and crafts gardens combined with unusual monastic ruins and a manor house
properties.locationText: North Yorkshire, Yorkshire and the Humber

properties.title: Muchelney Abbey
properties.description: Abbots’ luxury living on the Somerset Levels

properties.title: Netheravon Dovecote
properties.description: Charming and elegant 18th century brick dovecote, still with most of its 700 or more nesting boxes intact. Set in peaceful surroundings. External viewing only.

properties.title: Netley Abbey
properties.description: The most complete surviving Cistercian monastery in southern England, with almost all the walls of its 13th-century church still standing, along with many monastic buildings.

properties.title: Nine Ladies Stone Circle
properties.description: A small early Bronze Age stone circle of (actually) ten stones. Believed to be nine ladies turned to stone as a penalty for dancing on Sunday.

properties.title: Norham Castle
properties.description: Commanding a vital ford over the River Tweed, Norham was one of the strongest of the border castles, and the most often attacked by the Scots.

properties.title: North Elmham Chapel
properties.description: A place with an unusual story, told by graphic panels. The small Norman chapel here stood on the site of an earlier timber church, probably the Saxon cathedral of East Anglia.
properties.period_detail: Early Medieval (c. 410 - 1066 AD: Anglo-Saxon / Celtic / Viking)

properties.title: North Hinksey Conduit House
properties.description: Roofed conduit for Oxford's first water mains, constructed during the early 17th century.

properties.title: North Leigh Roman Villa
properties.description: The remains of a large, well built Roman courtyard villa. The most important feature is a nearly complete mosaic tile floor, patterned in reds and browns.

properties.title: Nunney Castle
properties.description: Picturesque moated castle built in the 1370s. Held for the King during the Civil War, falling to Parliamentarian cannon in 1645: the gun-damaged wall finally collapsing on Christmas Day 1910.

properties.title: Nympsfield Long Barrow
properties.description: Large Neolithic burial mound with spectacular views over the Severn Valley. Built by earliest farming communities in the Cotswolds almost 5,000 years ago. Internal chambers are uncovered for viewing.

properties.title: Odda's Chapel
properties.description: One of the most complete surviving Saxon churches in England, this chapel was built in 1056 by Earl Odda, and rediscovered in 1865 subsumed into a farmhouse. Nearby is the famous Saxon parish church.
properties.period_detail: Early Medieval (c. 410 - 1066 AD: Anglo-Saxon / Celtic / Viking)

properties.title: Offa's Dyke
properties.description: An earthwork roughly following the Welsh/English boundary consisting of a ditch and rampart. Origins shrouded in mystery but possibly built in response to events involving the Princes of Powys.

properties.title: Okehampton Castle
properties.description: One of Devon’s biggest and most picturesque castle.

properties.title: Old Blockhouse
properties.description: Substantial remains of a small 16th century gun tower protecting Old Grimsby harbour, vigorously defended during the Civil War.

properties.title: Old Gorhambury House
properties.description: The remains of a once immense mansion built in 1563-8 by Sir Nicholas Bacon, Queen Elizabeth’s Lord Keeper and visited by the queen on at least four occasions.

properties.title: Old Oswestry Hillfort
properties.description: The huge hillfort at Old Oswestry was probably the stronghold and principal settlement of an Iron Age tribe, with its 40 acres protected by formidable ramparts.

properties.title: Old Sarum
properties.description: Explore a vanished city
properties.period_detail: Iron Age / Roman / Norman motte & cathedral

properties.title: Old Soar Manor
properties.description: A small but complete portion of a stone manor house built about 1290. The first floor 'solar' private chamber, with attendant chapel and garderobe, stands over a vaulted undercroft.

properties.title: Old Wardour Castle
properties.description: Showpiece house to romantic ruin

properties.title: Orford Castle
properties.description: A fresh view of an ancient castle keep.

properties.title: Osborne
properties.description: Queen Victoria and Prince Albert’s beloved seaside palace

properties.title: Over Bridge
properties.description: A single-arch stone bridge spanning the River Severn, built in 1825-30 by the great engineer Thomas Telford.

properties.title: Pendennis Castle
properties.description: Adventures in hands-on history

properties.title: Penhallam Manor
properties.description: The low and grass-covered but complete ground-plan of a moated 13th-century manor house, in a delightful woodland setting.

properties.title: Penrith Castle
properties.description: Penrith Castle was begun at the end of the 14th century by Ralph Neville, who played a key role in defending this area against the Scots.

properties.title: Pevensey Castle
properties.description: From Roman fortress to Second World War defences

properties.title: Peveril Castle
properties.description: Spectacular hilltop castle that’s well worth the climb.

properties.title: Pickering Castle
properties.description: A classic medieval castle ruin near the North York Moors
properties.locationText: North Yorkshire, Yorkshire and the Humber

properties.title: Piel Castle
properties.description: The impressive ruins of a 14th-century castle with a massive keep, inner and outer baileys, and towered curtain walls still standing.

properties.title: Piercebridge Roman Bridge
properties.description: Stonework foundations, now marooned in a field, of a bridge which once led to Piercebridge Roman Fort.
properties.locationText: Borough of Darlington, Yorkshire and the Humber

properties.title: Pike Hill Signal Tower - Hadrian's Wall
properties.description: The remains of one of a network of signal towers predating Hadrian's Wall, Pike Hill was later joined to the Wall at an angle of 45 degrees.

properties.title: Planetrees Roman Wall - Hadrian's Wall
properties.description: A 35-metre length of narrow Wall on broad foundations, reflecting a change of policy during construction concerning the thickness of the wall.

properties.title: Poltross Burn Milecastle - Hadrian's Wall

properties.title: Rollright Stones

properties.title: Rufford Abbey

properties.title: Rushton Triangular Lodge
properties.description: One of England’s strangest buildings, packed with secret codes.

properties.title: Sandbach Crosses

properties.title: Sawley Abbey
properties.description: The remains of a Cistercian abbey founded in 1148, set on the banks of the Ribble against a backdrop of dramatic hills.

properties.title: Shrewsbury Flaxmill Maltings

properties.title: Silchester Roman City Walls and Amphitheatre
properties.description: Originally a tribal centre of the Iron Age Atrebates, Silchester became the large and important Roman town of Calleva Atrebatum.

properties.title: Sir Bevil Grenville's Monument
properties.description: Erected to commemorate the heroism of a Royalist commander and his Cornish pikemen at the Battle of Lansdown, 1643, this monument marks the spot where he fell.

properties.title: Skipsea Castle

properties.description: Remains of a wealthy Augustinian priory, originally founded at Portchester: once a famous place of pilgrimage. Only part of the refectory wall survives.

Yet recent surveys have revealed that the circles and cove were just part of a much more elaborate and important ritual site than had previously been imagined.

properties.title: Stanwick Iron Age Fortifications

properties.title: The Nine Stones
properties.description: Now in a wooded glade, this small prehistoric circle of nine standing stones was constructed around 4,000 years ago and is surrounded by a mysterious air. Winterbourne Poor Lot Barrows are nearby.

properties.title: The Sanctuary, Avebury
properties.description: Begun in about 3000 BC as a complex circle of timber posts, later replaced by stones. Its function is still mystifies: human bone finds with food remains point to elaborate death rites and ceremonies.

properties.description: The only surviving remains in England of a priory of Canons of the Holy Sepulchre, who aided pilgrims to Christ's tomb: the ruined nave of their 14th-century church, later used as a barn.
